web_evidence.title: No Man's Land by David Baldacci
web_evidence.note: BingeBooks' sustained sample presents Chapters 1–3 in third-person narration, first following Paul Rogers and then John Puller. BingeBooks identifies publisher feeds and Big Five partnerships, and its terms attribute hosted literary content to authors, publishers, or licensors, supporting treatment as an authorized sample.

web_evidence.note: The publisher page verifies the 2016 Grand Central edition and its parallel Puller and Rogers plotlines, but its synopsis grammar does not independently establish narrative person.

search_log: Searched “No Man's Land David Baldacci excerpt chapter 1 publisher,” “point of view third person narrator,” the author site, and Google Books.
Opened the Hachette publisher page, Pan Macmillan page, Publishers Weekly review, Google Books record, and BingeBooks excerpt; only the sustained BingeBooks preview was directly diagnostic.
Searched exact title/ISBN and exact passage text, locating a continuous preview covering Chapters 1–3 and confirming that the supplied Goodreads passages match the same work.

Searched title combinations with “third person,” “third-person,” “point of view,” and “multiple points of view”; results were dominated by unrelated works and yielded no credible explicit whole-book POV analysis.

Searched OverDrive and library catalogs for an authorized sample; a Reading District Libraries/OverDrive record offered “Read a sample,” but opening it returned HTTP 403, so it was not used as person evidence.
Targeted searches found no credible indication of epistolary form, a first-person frame, sustained second-person narration, or alternation between grammatical persons.

Independent audit checked BingeBooks' About, FAQ, and terms pages: the service states that it carries publisher-fed catalogs, including Hachette, and attributes its literary content to authors, publishers, or licensors, so the sustained sample remains Tier A despite the nonpublisher host.
person_note: The controlling narration is THIRD. The strongest interior excerpts sustain external narration around John Puller and Paul Rogers, while the licensed BingeBooks sample independently shows Chapters 1–3 using the same third-person method across both focal characters. In q01083, the isolated 'my mother' is locally attributable free-direct thought after the narration explicitly names Puller and introduces his questions; it is not evidence of a first-person narrator. Several weaker passages were reduced to unmarked because bare names or third-person subjects alone are not diagnostic. Confidence is medium because the only useful web prose covers the opening and the remaining web sources are metadata or synopsis. Independent audit: verified BingeBooks' publisher-feed/licensor basis, retained its Tier A status, corrected weak quote signals, and calibrated confidence consistently with other opening-only Baldacci cases.
